global.headline: HUANG IS REINSTATED AT NVIDIA AS WASHINGTON BLACKLISTS MEGASPEED
summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously on Monday to return Jensen Huang as chief executive, president and director, ten days after he resigned over an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom US officials allege spied for Beijing. Trump said he had "convinced" the board, which said its national-security investigation continues.

Hours later Commerce put Megaspeed International, registered in Singapore, on the entity list with two affiliates in Malaysia and Thailand; it now needs a licence to buy American chips. Bloomberg-cited trade records put its purchases of Nvidia's top accelerators at about S$1.01bn (US$787m) in November 2025 alone. Nvidia had put it on an internal "No Sell" list in June 2025, and Justice is running a criminal export-control case Commerce opened in 2024. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing; Scott Bessent said other agencies had favoured listing it "for months, but Commerce has the pen".

Nvidia closed up 31.48 per cent at S$211.26 (US$165.05), after rising as much as 36.6 per cent, adding S$1.22 trillion (US$952bn) of value in its best day since 2003. The Nasdaq rose 6.51 per cent to 24,089.56 and the S&P 500 4.73 per cent to 7,237.17, their best sessions since April 2025, a week after both lost over 8 per cent.
global.geopolitical: Washington did two contradictory things to one scandal on Monday: listed the counterparty as a security risk and restored the executive whose conduct exposed it. The chokepoint on Chinese access to compute is now personal rather than institutional, reversible by one phone call, and Beijing has watched that demonstrated.
global.socioeconomic: A trillion dollars moved on a single appointment, the clearest price yet on key-man risk in the AI trade. Retirement savings are now more exposed to one firm's governance than to any macroeconomic variable, and whoever sold into last week's slide missed Monday's rebound entirely.

global.headline: SENATE REPUBLICANS OPEN THE DOOR TO DEFUNDING THE IRAN WAR
summary: Senate Republican leaders signalled on Monday that they would consider the Democrats' demand to replenish the Pentagon while cutting off money for offensive operations against Iran. Appropriations chair Susan Collins is exploring language that funds weapons stockpiles but blocks offensive action; majority leader John Thune said he was open to negotiating; Armed Services chair Roger Wicker said Democrats could make their point "without tying the hands of the commander in chief".

Democrats, led here by Tim Kaine and Chris Van Hollen, want offensive action barred absent congressional authorisation while funds remain to defend troops and evacuate civilians; Tammy Duckworth says she will vote against any bill that does not cut the war off. Funding expires on 11 December with ten session days left after the Thanksgiving recess. Republicans hold 53 seats and need seven Democrats to break a filibuster; Trump has promised liberal use of his veto, so any restriction needs veto-proof margins. The Senate blocked a war-powers resolution to end hostilities last week.
global.geopolitical: For nine months Congress tried to constrain this war through war powers and failed every time. The attempt has moved to appropriations, the one instrument a president cannot ignore, and it is Republican committee chairs rather than backbenchers entertaining it.
global.socioeconomic: The trade on offer is money for depleted munitions stocks against a ban on using them offensively, putting defence-industrial orders and a pre-holiday shutdown on the same vote. Contractors waiting on replenishment now depend on a bargain over the war itself.

global.headline: A HACK OF RUSSIA'S OWN STATISTICS AGENCY PUTS ITS WAR DEAD ABOVE 700,000
summary: Meduza and Mediazona published on Monday an estimate that more than 700,000 Russian soldiers had died in Ukraine by late September 2026. The figure rests on Rosstat records taken by the pro-Ukrainian hacker groups Cyber Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow: the files show about 490,000 registered military deaths, and the outlets projected upward for the missing and for men killed but not yet recorded, since registration commonly lags six months or more.

They say they verified the files by matching record numbers and dates against Russia's inheritance register and against data leaked separately from registry offices. Earlier work this month on Rosstat material had put the toll above 400,000. Neither Moscow nor Rosstat has published a military death figure since the first weeks of the invasion.
global.geopolitical: Putin has fought this war on the premise that its cost need never be stated, and the number has come out of his own statistical apparatus rather than from Kyiv or NATO. That removes the deniability any further mobilisation depends on, while Moscow is being asked to trade territory in talks it has conceded nothing in.
global.socioeconomic: Seven hundred thousand deaths among working-age men is a labour-supply shock laid on a demographic decline Russia already could not reverse, and it falls on the regions that supplied the contract soldiers, not on Moscow.

global.headline: ISRAEL'S LEADERS NAME SETTLER ARSON AS "JEWISH TERRORISM"
summary: Settlers torched at least a dozen vehicles and several homes over the weekend in Deir al-Sudan, Deir Abu Mash'al and Kafr Malik, villages within a few kilometres of Ramallah, leaving Hebrew graffiti including "revenge"; no injuries were reported, and the military also received reports of an attack at At-Tuwani near Hebron.

By Monday the raids were the central argument in Israel's unresolved coalition fight. Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate to form a government, called them "Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word", said the country was close to unchecked anarchy and demanded action against violent settlers. Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned "a handful of extremists". Itamar Ben-Gvir, who holds the police portfolio, answered that Eisenkot was selling out to Arab parties. Netanyahu, still caretaker prime minister, had not addressed the criticism.
global.geopolitical: The West Bank has become the terrain on which this government is being formed, not a file the next one inherits. Eisenkot is using the phrase Israeli officials have spent years avoiding precisely because it commits whoever takes the police ministry to acting against the bloc Ben-Gvir speaks for.
global.socioeconomic: Burning vehicles and homes in olive-growing villages during the harvest destroys the assets smallholders farm with, not just the crop. With no prosecutions announced, the loss sits with households whose insurance and recourse are effectively nil.

global.headline: NEW YORK'S HIGHEST COURT CLEARS THE PLATFORMS OVER THE BUFFALO SHOOTING
summary: The New York Court of Appeals ruled four to three on Monday that Google, YouTube, Instagram, Reddit and Snapchat cannot be sued over the 2022 Tops supermarket shooting in Buffalo, in which ten Black shoppers were killed. The suits argued that the platforms' recommendation engines are defectively designed products that radicalised the gunman, Payton Gendron — a theory built to get around the federal immunity shielding platforms from what users post.

The majority held that the plaintiffs had not shown the attack was a "natural and foreseeable consequence" of the companies' design and operating choices. Claims against Amazon, Discord, 4chan and Twitch were dismissed the same day. Judge Jenny Rivera, dissenting, said a jury should decide whether the prevalence of mass shootings put the companies on notice that an allegedly defective product could trigger such violence.
global.geopolitical: The design-defect argument was the main route left for holding platforms liable in American courts, and it has failed in the state whose commercial bench others follow most closely. That widens the gap with Europe, where the Digital Services Act imposes design duties by statute rather than leaving them to a jury.
global.socioeconomic: Recommendation algorithms carry no priced tort exposure in the United States for what they surface, so the engagement economics driving them are untouched. The families' remaining avenue is legislation, which no state has passed in a form that survives review.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE AND CHINA CLOSE 29 DELIVERABLES AND OPEN TALKS ON CSFTA 4.0
summary: The 22nd Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation met in Singapore on Monday, co-chaired by DPM Gan Kim Yong and Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, and concluded 29 deliverables, the most in recent years. Negotiations were launched on a fourth upgrade of the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement, adding a digital-economy component covering cross-border data flows, digital trade, digital payments and AI cooperation and governance; Gan said it may take "a year or two". MOUs on trade in services, innovation, public health and food security were renewed, and JTC signed one with the Suzhou Industrial Park committee on embodied AI.

All three government-to-government projects were widened: Suzhou into bioscience, the Tianjin Eco-City beyond the city to the whole Jing-Jin-Ji region, and Chongqing towards the Pinglu Canal and the New International Land-Sea Trade Corridor, whose international cargo grew 25 per cent in the first ten months of 2026. Hainan became the first Chinese province cleared to send frozen and chilled poultry and shell eggs here, and was added as a pork source; food trade has more than doubled to over S$2.3bn last year from S$1bn in 2020. MAS announced renminbi measures including exploring China government bonds as eligible collateral.
singapore.geopolitical: Three days after PM Wong said in Beijing that Singapore can give Washington visibility over chips deployed here but cannot police re-exports, it has opened negotiations on a data-flows and AI-governance chapter with China. The hedge is becoming a treaty text — and on the same day a Singapore-registered firm went onto the US entity list.
singapore.socioeconomic: A first mainland province cleared for chilled poultry and eggs is real diversification for a country importing over 90 per cent of its food, and a doubled S$2.3bn food trade makes China a structural rather than marginal source. For firms the open question is whether the digital chapter arrives inside the two years Gan allowed.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE REGRETS COP31 AND FALLS BACK ON ITS CARBON-MARKET ROUTE
summary: Grace Fu said on Monday that Singapore regretted parties could not agree the Antalya Pact, which fell short of some countries' expectations while holding positive elements, and hoped the setback would not pull nations apart; Singapore will work with the incoming Ethiopian COP32 presidency. Analysts told the Straits Times the collapse is unlikely to derail Singapore's own priorities, while noting the carbon tax rate set for 2028 to 2030 is exposed to the lack of international consensus.

The domestic carbon tax rose from S$25 to S$45 a tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent this year, with S$50 to S$80 set as the 2030 range, and liable firms may offset up to 5 per cent of taxable emissions with international credits bought under bilateral agreements — including one signed with Zambia at Antalya on 18 November. Separately, the Singapore-based Tsao Family Foundation and Tara Climate Foundation launched a S$3.9m (US$3m) El Nino Resilience Fund on Monday, US$850,000 of it secured, for heat insurance for informal workers and drought water storage, first disbursements due in mid-December.
singapore.geopolitical: Singapore's climate position runs through Article 6 rather than the cover decision, so a conference that could not name fossil fuels costs it less than it costs petitioners for adaptation finance. Its exposure is different: bilateral credit deals need willing counterparties, and a stalled process hands host countries leverage over price.
singapore.socioeconomic: Industry here waits on a domestic decision, not an international one: the 2028-to-2030 tax path is set in Singapore and the credits that soften it are bought one country at a time. A S$3.9m philanthropic fund is meanwhile the scale at which adaptation money actually moves, after a text that would have numbered it failed.

singapore.headline: A ONE-OFF PROPERTY TAX REBATE FOR EVERY OWNER-OCCUPIED HOME IN 2027
summary: The Finance Ministry and IRAS announced on Monday a one-off 2027 property tax rebate for all owner-occupied homes: 15 per cent for HDB flats and 10 per cent for private residential properties, capped at S$100 against this year's S$500 private cap. It is offset automatically against bills issued by December, and owner-occupiers of one- and two-room flats continue to pay no property tax at all.

From 1 March 2027 the annual value thresholds used to means-test social support rise: the first tier from S$21,000 to S$24,000, and the upper limit of the second tier from S$31,000 to S$32,000, with eligibility for 2027 benefits assessed on a property's 2026 annual value. IRAS illustrated the rebate with a private property owing S$7,500 in 2027 tax, where the capped S$100 leaves S$7,400 payable.
singapore.geopolitical: Raising the annual value bands matters more than the rebate. Means-testing here is anchored to property values, so when annual values rise with market rents households drift out of eligibility without their circumstances changing; the S$3,000 first-tier move corrects that drift rather than extending support.
singapore.socioeconomic: The rebate is small and tilted downward — 15 per cent uncapped for flats against S$100 for private homes — so the transfer is modest for most owners and near-symbolic at the top. The threshold change is the durable part: it decides who qualifies for subsidies long after a one-year rebate expires.

singapore.headline: HDB PLANS A PASIR RIS NEIGHBOURHOOD AND KEEPS 13 HECTARES OF IT WILD
summary: HDB released a conceptual plan on Monday for a neighbourhood of public and private housing on a 36ha coastal site along Pasir Ris Drive 4, zoned residential since the 1980 Master Plan. About 13ha of existing habitat is to be retained: roughly 8ha of intertidal flats, seagrass beds and mangroves, and 5ha of forest kept as a buffer, with a 15m linear park along Sungei Loyang.

An environmental impact assessment by Tembusu Asia Consulting covered the full 36ha and nature groups were consulted; a monitoring and management plan will run through construction. Lester Tan of the Nature Society Singapore called the forest retention a good effort but said the patch may be too small to support breeding greater mousedeer and Sunda pangolin. Public feedback closes on 20 December.
singapore.geopolitical: A site zoned for housing 46 years ago is released only with an impact assessment, a retained habitat share and a consultation window — the practical shape of the trade-off on a land-constrained island. What the plan does not settle is whether retention at this scale conserves species or only scenery.
singapore.socioeconomic: Seaside land is the scarcest housing supply Singapore has, and a mixed public-private neighbourhood changes who can live on a coast otherwise priced privately. The cost is carried by the 23ha built over, and by the species whose range the retained 13ha may be too narrow to hold.

word.definition: The elevation of a person to divine rank; by extension, the moment at which someone is treated as the perfect and indispensable embodiment of a thing.
word.etymology: From Greek apotheosis, from apotheoun, to make a god of, from apo-, utterly, and theos, god; through Late Latin into English in the seventeenth century, first for the Roman senate's practice of declaring a dead emperor divine.
word.example: Ten days after resigning in disgrace, Jensen Huang was restored by a unanimous board at a president's urging and handed back S$1.22 trillion of market value in one session — an apotheosis performed by the same institutions that had just removed him.
